headline: Majors underwater, momentum split, shorts getting wiped while whales pull coins to storage.
paragraphs: The regime is bearish across the board. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and ADA are all trading below their 200-day simple moving averages, and none of them have a golden cross in place. BNB is also underwater on the 200-day line. The only asset with any momentum lift is BNB, which has MACD above signal, but it too sits below its trend line and has not reclaimed the 200-day. That is six assets below trend and one with a technical spark but no trend confirmation. Bitcoin is 48.9% down from its 12-month high of $124,739, Ethereum is 61.2% down, and the further you move down the cap stack, the worse it gets: Solana is 70.2% down, ADA is 79.9% down, DOGE is 75.7% down. This is a market that has surrendered its long-term frame.

Momentum tells a conflicted story against this downtrend. BTC and ETH both have RSI-14 in the neutral zone (49.1 and 51.5 respectively), neither overbought nor oversold, while their MACD lines sit below signal. Solana and XRP are in similar straits: RSI below 50, MACD below signal. But BNB shows RSI at 57.7 with MACD above signal, a small pocket of internal strength in a sea of weakness. ADA is the outlier: RSI is 68.1, technically overbought, with MACD above signal and a 7-day move of +17.76% and 30-day move of +22.55%, making it a divergence in the other direction. The crowd is in Extreme Fear (value 25, 30-day range 20 to 33), near the low end of its recent window, yet Bitcoin's 24-hour move is +0.49% and Ethereum is +0.62%. Weakness in trend paired with flat-to-slightly-positive daily price action and overbought fear gauge is a classic late-stage capitulation posture: the money has already moved, and price is confirming it slowly.

Positioning in derivatives reveals the real tension. Bitcoin funding is positive at 1 basis point per 8 hours (annualized to 11%), which means longs are still paying to hold, but the rate is calm, not urgent. Open interest is $2.02 billion, substantial, and the long-to-short ratio is 1.64, meaning there are 64% more longs than shorts on the books. In the last 23 hours, 979 liquidations occurred: $1.36 million in longs wiped, $6.23 million in shorts wiped. That is a 4.6-to-1 ratio of shorts to longs getting liquidated. The same pattern holds across ETH, SOL, XRP, and DOGE: the longs-to-shorts ratios are high (1.97 for ETH, 2.67 for SOL, 3.09 for XRP, 4.84 for DOGE), and the liquidation tally is skewed toward shorts. On SOL, shorts accounted for $633,555 of the $750,277 in liquidations; on DOGE, shorts were $204,956 out of $209,644. This is a crowded long trade being tested, and the shorts are breaking faster than the longs. Funding is not expensive, but the ratio structure is precarious.

Whale flows over the last 48 hours paint a clear picture: $103.1 million in Bitcoin moved off exchanges, with the biggest single move being $51.55 million from Coinbase institutional. Stablecoin flows are harder to read at first glance because USDT had both inflow ($119.88 million to Bitfinex) and outflow ($133.4 million and $119.82 million from Bitfinex, both large), resulting in a net negative buying power of $133.3 million. That net negative number means coins leaving exchanges are not being met with fresh stablecoin entry; instead, the whale wallet is pulling Bitcoin to cold storage and doing so while drawing down the stablecoin float. Over the last four weeks, whale flows have swung from a net $367 million inflow (two weeks ago) to a net $1.12 billion outflow (most recent week), a complete reversal. This is not panic selling; this is accumulation into cold storage during capitulation. The stablecoin float stands at $305.77 billion, down 0.88% over the month, modest but also directional: dry powder is not building, and the whales are not waiting to buy cheaper.

Sentiment and flows are in open conflict. The Fear and Greed gauge sits at 25 (Extreme Fear), the crowd is terrified, and yet Bitcoin saw a $170.1 million inflow on August 3rd (the latest ETF print), with a five-session net of $120.2 million positive, though only one of the last five sessions was positive (same_direction_days: 1). Ethereum ETF flows went negative: minus $11.9 million on the latest day and minus $13.6 million over five sessions. Traditional finance is not all-in; the real accumulation is happening in whale wallets pulling coins to custody. The total market cap is $2.27 trillion, up 1.39% in 24 hours, while Bitcoin dominance sits at 56.4%, a position of strength relative to alts. The daily moves are muted, but the weekly picture for BTC is flat (minus 0.84%), and the 30-day is also flat (minus 0.25%). This is a market grinding sideways at the bottom of a massive drawdown, with insiders accumulating and the crowd frozen in fear.

Watch for a funding flip on Bitcoin: if the 8-hour rate goes negative, longs are no longer willing to pay to hold, and capitulation has reached the marginal seller. Watch whether the outflow of Bitcoin from exchanges sustains or reverses; a return to inflows while whales are still pulling would mean retail is chasing. Watch whether BTC reclaims the 200-day line, which would be the first technical confirmation that the trend is not purely down. Finally, watch the ETH outflow pattern: if institutional Bitcoin buying persists but Ethereum keeps seeing net redemptions, that is a signal that the bid is selective and Bitcoin-specific, not a risk-on macro turn. The tape is patient, but the positioning is extreme.
